english_before: Genera of a split surface
english_after: Genera of a reducible surface
reported_problem: The Italian refers to a reducible surface, a union of component surfaces, rather than to a split surface.
reason: In Enriques a 'superficie spezzata' is a surface broken up into several components, that is a reducible surface, and 'split surface' is not an established English term for this.

english_before: can be represented in a simple way on a plane
english_after: can be represented one-to-one on a plane
reported_problem: Here 'in modo semplice' specifies a one-to-one representation, not merely an uncomplicated procedure.
reason: 'Rappresentare in modo semplice' means a one-to-one representation of the neighbourhood on the plane, as realized by the one-to-one projection of the osculating paraboloid, not a representation made in an uncomplicated way.

english_before: a $(2n-2)$-fold point, near which, and facing it, there are $n-1$ double points on a branch
english_after: a $(2n-2)$-fold point with $n-1$ infinitely near double points proximate to it, on a branch
reported_problem: 'Fronteggianti' specifies that the infinitely near points are proximate to $O$, a technical relation not conveyed by 'facing it'.
reason: 'Vicini e fronteggianti' denotes infinitely near points proximate to the $(2n-2)$-fold point, a technical relation that 'near which, and facing it' does not convey.

english_before: change the neighborhood of this point into a line which forms part
english_after: change the neighborhood of this point into a curve which forms part
reported_problem: 'Linea' here denotes a curve, not necessarily a straight line, so the English adds an unwarranted restriction.
reason: Here 'linea' is the curve into which a plane birational transformation turns the neighbourhood of its fundamental point, not necessarily a straight line.

english_before: not composed of an involution
english_after: not composed with an involution
reported_problem: The Italian excludes a series that factors through an involution, which requires the technical expression “composed with,” not “composed of.”
reason: Composta con una involuzione is the technical expression for a series composed with an involution, which composed of misrenders.

english_before: as many 3-fold points near these in given directions
english_after: as many 3-fold points infinitely near these in given directions
reason: Vicini a questi in direzioni date denotes the triple points infinitely near the assigned ones (the second triple points of the [3,3] points), so near must read infinitely near.

english_before: describing arbitrary lines (closed or open)
english_after: describing arbitrary curves (closed or open)
reason: On p. 195 the linee described by the moving branch points in the x-plane are arbitrary paths, that is curves, not straight lines.

english_before: remain open and free lines, not crossing one another
english_after: remain open and free curves, not crossing one another
reason: On p. 195 the loops OA_i are required to remain open curves (linee aperte e sciolte), which are not straight.

english_before: the two lines \(OA_1\) and \(OA_2\), having in common the end point
english_after: the two curves \(OA_1\) and \(OA_2\), having in common the end point
reason: On p. 196 le due linee are the loops OA_1 and OA_2, which share an end point and bound a region, so they are curves and not straight lines.

english_before: so that these lines can be brought infinitely near to each other
english_after: so that these curves can be brought infinitely near to each other
reason: On p. 196 codeste linee are the same loops OA_1 and OA_2 and hence curves.

english_before: the two aforesaid lines, which come to have the common end point
english_after: the two aforesaid curves, which come to have the common end point
reason: On p. 197 le due linee anzidette are the loops OA_r and OA_s and hence curves.

english_before: will form a closed line bounding a surface
english_after: will form a closed curve bounding a surface
reason: On p. 197 una linea chiusa enclosing other branch points is a closed curve, not a straight line.

english_before: one can always bring the line \(OA_s\) infinitely near to \(OA_r\)
english_after: one can always bring the curve \(OA_s\) infinitely near to \(OA_r\)
reason: On p. 197 la linea OA_s is the loop deformed by continuity across branch points and hence a curve.

english_before: containing $\infty^{p_g-p_a}$ series of non-equivalent linear systems
english_after: containing series of $\infty^{p_g-p_a}$ non-equivalent linear systems
reported_problem: The Italian describes series of dimension $p_g-p_a$, whereas the English counts the series rather than the linear systems within them.
reason: In the Italian serie $\infty^{p_g-p_a}$ the exponent gives the dimension of each series (each consists of $\infty^{p_g-p_a}$ non-equivalent linear systems), whereas the English places it before series and so counts the series instead.

english_before: a continuous series of nets of non-equivalent curves
english_after: a continuous series of non-equivalent nets of curves
reason: In reti di curve non equivalenti the non-equivalence holds between the nets of the continuous series (all curves of one net being equivalent), so by the same rule as for equivalent groups of curves the English should read non-equivalent nets of curves.

english_before: which we have seen to be composed of the \(g_2^1\)
english_after: which we have seen to be composed with the \(g_2^1\)
reason: Composta con la g_2^1 is the technical phrase for a series composed with the involution g_2^1, not composed of it.

english_before: This series is composed of the \(g_2^1\), because otherwise
english_after: This series is composed with the \(g_2^1\), because otherwise
reason: Composta colla g_2^1 likewise means the series is composed with the involution g_2^1, not composed of it.

english_before: but composed of an involution of the 2\textsuperscript{o} order
english_after: but composed with an involution of the 2\textsuperscript{o} order
reason: Composto con una involuzione means composed with an involution, not composed of one.

english_before: are generally irreducible to one another by birational transformations
english_after: are generally not transformable into one another by birational transformations
reason: Irriducibili per trasformazioni birazionali here means the surfaces cannot be transformed into one another birationally, not that they are irreducible.

english_before: corresponding to different values of $\pi$ $(>1)$ are in general irreducible.
english_after: corresponding to different values of $\pi$ $(>1)$ are in general birationally inequivalent to one another.
reported_problem: The assertion concerns mutual birational inequivalence for different values of $\pi$, not the irreducibility of each surface.
reason: Said of the surfaces for different values of pi, irriducibili means that they cannot be transformed birationally into one another, not that each surface is irreducible.

english_before: are in general irreducible by birational transformations
english_after: are in general birationally inequivalent to one another
reported_problem: The Italian asserts that the surfaces are not birationally transformable into one another, whereas the English fails to express this mutual inequivalence.
reason: Irriducibili per trasformazioni birazionali means not transformable into one another by birational transformations, which irreducible by birational transformations does not say.

english_before: two irreducible types of $F_{16}$
english_after: two birationally inequivalent types of $F_{16}$
reported_problem: Here the Italian distinguishes mutually birationally inequivalent types rather than asserting the irreducibility of each type.
reason: The two types of F_16 cannot be transformed into one another, so irriducibili here means birationally inequivalent, not irreducible.

english_before: both depending on 19 moduli and irreducible to each other.
english_after: both depending on 19 moduli and birationally inequivalent to each other.
reason: Fra loro irriducibili, said of the s-fold multiple surface and the simple surface, means that they cannot be transformed birationally into each other, not that they are irreducible.

english_before: and irreducible to them, were indicated by
english_after: and birationally inequivalent to them, were indicated by
reason: Ad esse irriducibili means that Castelnuovo's surfaces cannot be transformed birationally into the quartic surfaces, not that they are irreducible.

english_before: the quadric cone osculating the latter at $O$
english_after: the quadric cone osculating this surface section at $O$
reported_problem: The Italian refers to the surface section, whereas 'the latter' points to the tangent space $S_3$.
reason: The feminine questa can only refer to the surface section (spazio $S_3$ is masculine), whereas 'the latter' in the English points to the tangent space $S_3$.

english_before: free from base points or base lines
english_after: free from base points or base curves
reported_problem: Here 'linee base' means base curves, not necessarily straight lines.
reason: The linee base of a linear system of surfaces on a threefold are base curves, not straight lines.

english_before: the number of the continuous systems of independent curves traced on the surface
english_after: the number of independent continuous systems of curves traced on the surface
reported_problem: The independence concerns the continuous systems of curves, not the curves within each system.
reason: Like tracciati, which can agree only with sistemi, indipendenti qualifies the continuous systems (the base number counts independent systems), whereas the English makes the curves of each system independent.

english_before: two points \(O_1\) and \(O_2\) near to it
english_after: two points \(O_1\) and \(O_2\) proximate to it
reason: Prossimi ad esso is the technical term for points infinitely near to O and proximate to it, which the vague near to it does not convey.

english_before: but does not possess a double line
english_after: but does not possess a double curve
reported_problem: The Italian excludes any double curve, not merely a straight double line.
reason: Linea doppia here means a double curve of any kind (one would give infinitely many pairs of incident generators), not a straight double line.

english_before: describe groups of equivalent curves
english_after: describe equivalent groups of curves
reported_problem: Equivalence applies to the groups of curves, not to the individual curves, which are non-equivalent.
reason: It is the groups of i curves C (the sums C_i, as in case b) that are equivalent to one another, while the individual curves C are non-equivalent.

english_before: the lines \(I=\mathrm{const.}\)
english_after: the curves \(I=\mathrm{const.}\)
reason: The linee I=cost. are the level curves of the integral I on the surface, not straight lines, so linea must be rendered as curve.

english_before: \(\infty^1\) pairs of equivalent curves
english_after: \(\infty^1\) equivalent pairs of curves
reported_problem: Equivalence applies to the pairs of curves, not to the individual curves, which have just been stated to be non-equivalent.
reason: The curves of the family are mutually non-equivalent, so the equivalent objects are the pairs, which form a g_2^1 on the elliptic family as p. 376 explains.

english_before: series of pairs of equivalent elements
english_after: series of equivalent pairs of elements
reported_problem: Equivalence applies to the pairs as degree-two divisors on the elliptic entity, not to their individual elements.
reason: The elements of the elliptic entity are not equivalent to one another; the pairs are, and they therefore form a g_2^1.

english_before: cutting the \(K\) in groups of equivalent points
english_after: cutting the \(K\) in equivalent groups of points
reported_problem: The groups of points cut on \(K\) are equivalent, not the individual points.
reason: The groups of points cut on the K by the two parapluricanonical curves are equivalent, not the individual points.

english_before: composite with the rational curves of a pencil
english_after: composed with the rational curves of a pencil
reason: A system composto con the curves of a pencil takes the standard term composed with (as for composto con un'involuzione), not composite with.

english_before: composite with the curves of the pencil
english_after: composed with the curves of the pencil
reason: The Italian composto con le curve del fascio takes the standard term composed with, as for composto con un'involuzione.

english_before: another \textit{similar type}, irreducible by birational transformations
english_after: another \textit{similar type}, not transformable into it by birational transformations
reason: Said of a second type, "irriducibile per trasformazioni birazionali" means that it cannot be carried into the first by birational transformations (birationally inequivalent), not that it is irreducible.
